The one place the technique did apply — five official binaries in AR and NC that carry a digest and no repository path — it was run, and all five resolved in mounted master_library.

All six already printed exactly that at the assigned base, before any change. That verifier does not measure SOURCE_IDENTITY, so a COMPLETED row carrying nine zero counters would have been true and meaningless for this cohort — it would assert a repair the named evidence cannot see.

environmentDefectFoundAndCorrected.what: git worktree add inherits core.sparseCheckout from the parent repository. The inherited cone excludes /data/* except /data/rcap-grade-a/, so data/record-clearing/, data/rcap-ledger/ and data/rcap-all50/ were absent from a freshly created worktree while remaining tracked in git.
environmentDefectFoundAndCorrected.howItPresented: the first rehash pass reported all six shared committed records ABSENT — a universal negative over files that are tracked and present in HEAD
environmentDefectFoundAndCorrected.whyItMatters: a lane that trusts that pass concludes every source is missing and records six false BLOCKED_SOURCE rows. This is the same broken-denominator shape the corpus index guards against, arriving through git configuration rather than through custody mounting. It is very likely the cause of the AR verifier's own caveat that the ACIC binaries 'were not reachable in this sparse checkout'.
environmentDefectFoundAndCorrected.correction: git sparse-checkout set was widened to include /data/record-clearing/, /data/rcap-ledger/ and /data/rcap-all50/ before any digest was believed. Worktree-local configuration only; no tracked file changed.
environmentDefectFoundAndCorrected.recommendation: lane setup instructions should widen the sparse cone explicitly, or lanes should assert that a known-tracked path is present on disk before treating any absence as evidence

determinationsForTheOwner.question: Should a shared committed record that many families pin by whole-file SHA-256 be allowed to drift without re-pinning every dependent receipt?
determinationsForTheOwner.measured: Across 357 family receipts: data/record-clearing/legal-design-packet-set-manifests.json is referenced by 64, route-obligation-candidate.json by 52, legal-design-track-registry.json by 27, legal-design-specifications.json by 17, and data/rcap-ledger/completed-output-counsel-manifest.json by 6. Any commit touching one of these invalidates every pin over it at once.
determinationsForTheOwner.why: CT's SOURCE_IDENTITY failure was caused by a Kansas/Virginia bookkeeping edit to a shared ledger. The verifiers themselves observed that 'the drift is national, not Oklahoman' and 'not Washingtonian'. This is a recurring, self-inflicted class: it will keep re-firing across dozens of families every time a shared record is edited.
options: bind the anchored subtree rather than the whole file, so an unrelated edit elsewhere in the record cannot invalidate a pin
keep whole-file pins but add a factory check that re-pins every dependent receipt in the same commit that edits a shared record
accept the drift and treat identityRefresh as routine maintenance

determinationsForTheOwner.question: Five of these six families are held at FAIL_REPAIR_REQUIRED by a verdict their receipts have already answered. What re-opens them?
determinationsForTheOwner.measured: AR, NC, NV, OK and WA each have every pin recomputing exactly at 1dabf8cc6, and all five already print PASS_COMPLETE with nine counters at zero. Their FAIL_REPAIR_REQUIRED verdicts were read at bases that predate the repairs FIX01/02/03/04/06/08 landed on 2026-09-04 and 2026-09-05.

Sending another repair lane at them produces no change and no evidence.

determinationsForTheOwner.question: Was this cohort dispatched against the right diagnosis?
determinationsForTheOwner.measured: The dispatch identified the deciding technique as content-hash resolution against mounted custodies for sources whose declared paths point into absent custodies. No family in this cohort is blocked that way. Five are stale-pin drift over committed records; one is the same drift uncured. The dispatch's stated bar (PASS_COMPLETE, nine zero counters) was already green on all six before any work and is structurally blind to SOURCE_IDENTITY.
determinationsForTheOwner.why: A lane that took the dispatch at face value would have indexed the custodies, found nothing relevant, and had a live choice between reporting six false BLOCKED_SOURCE rows or reporting six COMPLETED rows with nine honest zero counters that prove nothing. Both are wrong, and the second is the more dangerous because it reads as success.
determinationsForTheOwner.recommendation: repair dispatches for SOURCE_IDENTITY should name a bar that measures source identity, and should carry the verifier's finding body rather than only the obligation name

determinationsForTheOwner.question: Who may move a released grant onto a lane?
determinationsForTheOwner.measured: All six families in this cohort were granted to other FIX lanes; --assert FIX12 exits 8 GRANTED_ELSEWHERE on every one. claim.mjs --transfer would have succeeded mechanically, and the ledger shows the earlier FIX12 cohort was dispatched exactly that way — but every such record is stamped with a Captain dispatch reason, and grant() hardcodes grantedBy: Captain.
determinationsForTheOwner.thisLaneRead: that choosing the destination of a grant is a dispatch act, not a worker act, and that a lane transferring six grants onto itself is precisely what the fail-closed gate exists to prevent. This lane therefore wrote no family and stopped.
determinationsForTheOwner.ifTheOwnerDisagrees: the CT repair is fully specified in this return and can be applied in minutes by whoever legitimately holds the grant
